PROBLEM: An authorized model request must cross exactly one wire send, then recover (account rotation / model fallback) without the recovery path inventing new authorization, and every attempt must return a typed outcome the caller can turn into a receipt.
MECHANISM: ProviderExecutionPolicy { allowAccountRotation, allowModelFallback, expectedConnectionId? } (lines 31-35) is passed into the pipeline; sendProviderAttempt performs the single wire send while account/model recovery is separated from it. Outcomes are typed ProviderExecutionOutcome { kind: 'response' | 'error' } (lines 37-53). A lease fence (leaseMismatch, lines 184-190; asserted at line 302 and 554) guarantees the connection the policy pinned is the connection that sent. Failed upstream responses teach the rate limiter before any retry/rotation. Retry budget is hard-capped: maxAttemptsFor gives Codex 3 attempts, all other providers 1 (lines 307-319, 330-377). Model fallback is gated on policy.allowModelFallback (line 517) and a triedModels set prevents cycles (lines 79, 122, 532). [Evidence: open-sse/handlers/chatCore/providerExecutionPipeline.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Authorization enters the pipeline as immutable policy; the pipeline may only select within policy.allowAccountRotation / policy.allowModelFallback / expectedConnectionId. The wire connection that sends is always the policy-pinned connection (lease fence).
FAILURE_MODEL: If expectedConnectionId mismatches the managed lease, the pipeline returns a typed lease_error without sending (lines 184-190, 302). Rate-limiter teaching failures do not block recovery. Unknown failure classes fall to the generic error outcome, never to an untyped exception crossing the seam.
SECURITY_MODEL: Credentials are accessed through PipelineConnectionContext getters (lines 63-74), never serialized into the outcome; only connectionId/model/outcome metadata leave the seam. No prompt bodies are logged by the pipeline itself.
SCALING_MODEL: State per attempt is O(1) (policy struct, tried-set, connection ctx). The pipeline adds no hot-path I/O beyond the single upstream send plus limiter teaching. Concurrent attempts are bounded by the caller's semaphore (line 28 _accountSemaphoreRelease).
CRX_ANALOG: Direct analog of the CRX execution seam: AuthorizedModelRequest enters as immutable ProviderExecutionPolicy; the pipeline is the ROUTE step; each sendProviderAttempt is a ProviderAttempt; the typed response|error outcome is the raw material for a durable ExecutionReceipt.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must (a) snapshot the full authorization envelope (policy version/hash, authorized provider/model/account/capability bounds) into the receipt, (b) persist every attempt durably rather than returning only the final outcome, and (c) guarantee the candidate set entering the pipeline was already authorized upstream. OmniRoute assumes the caller authorized; CRX must make that assumption a verified invariant.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium. The pipeline shape ports cleanly, but CRX must add durable per-attempt receipts, policy snapshotting, and a verified authorized-candidate precondition.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High. This is the closest existing implementation of the MODEL REQUEST -> POLICY -> ROUTE -> PROVIDER -> RECEIPT seam: immutable policy in, typed outcome out, recovery without re-authorization.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if a code path in the pipeline sends to a connection not covered by expectedConnectionId, or if model fallback executes when policy.allowModelFallback is false. Test: pin expectedConnectionId to a bogus id, stub the wire, and assert lease_error with zero upstream sends; then call with allowModelFallback=false and an unavailable model and assert no fallback attempt is made.

PROBLEM: Adding a new model provider (cloud, aggregator, local, or coding-agent CLI) must not require touching routing, policy, or receipt logic; the provider surface must be data-driven and swappable.
MECHANISM: Three independent layers: (1) declarative registration - open-sse/config/providers/index.ts imports ~290 per-provider modules from open-sse/config/providers/registry/<name>/index.ts (e.g. anthropic, ollama-cloud, bedrock, g4f-ollama), each exporting a provider descriptor; (2) execution - open-sse/executors/base.ts plus per-provider executors under open-sse/executors/ (216 files) implement the wire send against the descriptor; (3) translation - open-sse/translator/registry.ts keeps from:to protocol translators (e.g. claude-to-openai) keyed by makeKey(from,to) with register/getRequestTranslator/getResponseTranslator. Routing code consumes descriptors, never provider internals. [Evidence: open-sse/config/providers/index.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/executors/base.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/translator/registry.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Routing and policy layers never import provider internals; all provider-specific behavior is behind the descriptor / executor / translator interfaces. A provider that cannot express itself through the descriptor cannot be routed to.
FAILURE_MODEL: A missing translator registration returns undefined (registry.get) and the caller must handle absence explicitly; there is no implicit default translation. A malformed provider descriptor fails at registration/import time, not per-request.
SECURITY_MODEL: Provider credentials live in the connection/executor layer and are never part of the descriptor or the translator registry. New providers add no new secret-handling paths if they reuse the base executor.
SCALING_MODEL: Registration is O(N) at startup for N providers; per-request cost is a map lookup. Translators are pure functions with no retained state. The registry itself is unbounded only in the number of supported providers, not in traffic.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX PROVIDER step: a replaceable provider/driver registry where adding Ollama, a cloud API, or a coding-agent-compatible endpoint is a descriptor plus an executor, without changing POLICY or ROUTE.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must add capability declarations to the descriptor (tools, structured output, reasoning, context window, data residency) so ROUTE can filter on capability compatibility, not just name. OmniRoute descriptors carry pricing/metadata; CRX needs typed capability contracts for fallback safety.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low-Medium. The layering pattern is directly reusable; CRX must define its own descriptor schema with capability contracts.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High. Prevents the execution seam from calcifying around one provider API shape; makes 'replaceable execution seam' structurally true.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if routing or policy code imports a concrete provider module (e.g. open-sse/executors/anthropic) directly instead of going through the descriptor/executor interface. Test: static import analysis from autoCombo/scoring, engine, and the pipeline - any direct provider import fails the test.

PROBLEM: Providers speak different wire protocols (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Responses API). The execution seam must normalize an authorized canonical request into each provider's wire format and normalize the response back, without leaking provider quirks into routing.
MECHANISM: A from:to keyed registry (makeKey(from,to); register(from,to,requestFn?,responseFn?); getRequestTranslator/getResponseTranslator) holds pure translation functions: RequestTranslator(model, body, stream?, credentials?) -> unknown and ResponseTranslator(chunk, state) -> unknown. Concrete pairs like claude-to-openai and antigravity-to-openai live under open-sse/translator/request/ and /response/. Helpers normalize tool calls, schemas, max-tokens, system hoisting, and strict schema coercion (open-sse/translator/helpers/*). [Evidence: open-sse/translator/registry.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/translator/request/claude-to-openai.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/translator/request/antigravity-to-openai.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Translation is total and pure: the same canonical request always produces the same wire body; translators never perform I/O, never read credentials stores, and never consult routing state.
FAILURE_MODEL: An unregistered pair yields undefined and must be handled by the caller; a translator that throws is a translation failure, not a provider failure, and must not be charged to provider health (cf. accountFallback's internal-vs-provider distinction).
SECURITY_MODEL: Credentials may be passed to the request translator for header construction but must never be persisted by it or echoed into logs/traces.
SCALING_MODEL: Pure functions: zero retained state, O(request size) work. Registry size is bounded by protocol pairs, not traffic.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX PROVIDER step normalization: canonical AuthorizedModelRequest in, provider wire format out, provider chunks back into canonical receipt fields. Keeps ROUTE provider-agnostic.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must define the canonical request/response schema (the 'one wire shape') and require every provider driver to ship a bidirectional translator; OmniRoute grew translators organically per provider pair.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low. The registry shape and helper taxonomy can be lifted almost verbatim; CRX defines its canonical schema.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-High. Without protocol normalization the 'replaceable provider' claim is fiction; this is the mechanical piece that makes it real.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if any translator performs network I/O, reads the DB, or consults routing/scoring state. Test: run all registered translators in a sandbox with network and DB stubs that throw; any throw from the stub fails the test.

PROBLEM: One provider credential failing (429, 401, quota) must not take down routing; accounts must be selected, cooled down, retried with backoff, and health-scored, while internal executor bugs must never be charged to the provider.
MECHANISM: accountFallback.ts is a large typed error-classification and cooldown subsystem: provider-specific error-pattern signals (ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED_SIGNALS line 211, CREDITS_EXHAUSTED_SIGNALS 238, OAUTH_INVALID_TOKEN_SIGNALS 274, MODEL_PERMANENTLY_UNAVAILABLE_PATTERNS 297, RATE_LIMIT_TEXT_PATTERNS 457), per-model lockout with cooldown selection (lockModel line 770, selectLockoutCooldownMs line 822, lockModelIfPerModelQuota 980), failure-count decay (decayModelFailureCount line 1028), filterAvailableAccounts (line 2381) removing excluded/rate-limited accounts, and getAccountHealth (line 2503) computing a 0-100 score. It explicitly distinguishes internal executor contract violations from provider failures so providers are not punished for internal bugs. [Evidence: open-sse/services/accountFallback.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: A provider/account is only de-preferenced or excluded on the basis of observed provider-side failure signals; internal errors never degrade provider health. Excluded accounts can re-enter only via cooldown expiry or explicit clearing.
FAILURE_MODEL: Connection-cooldown persistence is best-effort: DB failures are swallowed, so cooldown state can silently drift after a DB outage. This is the mechanism's weakest point.
SECURITY_MODEL: No credential material is stored in cooldown state; only connection/account ids and failure counters. Error-text pattern matching operates on provider error bodies - ensure bodies are not persisted with credentials.
SCALING_MODEL: Cooldown maps and lockout entries are bounded (evictModelLockoutOverflow line 755); per-request selection cost is O(accounts). State is in-memory with best-effort DB persistence.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE step account selection: within the authorized account set, select the healthy account, cool down failures, and record per-attempt health - but CRX must make cooldown state durable and typed rather than best-effort.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must replace swallowed DB failures with typed persistence outcomes in the receipt (attempt still valid; state write failed -> explicit gap marker), and bind cooldown entries to the authorized account set so a cooled-down pool can never resurrect a policy-forbidden account.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium. Classification patterns and cooldown math port well; persistence semantics must be rebuilt fail-closed.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High. Per-account health with cooldown is the difference between a router that flaps and one that degrades gracefully under partial provider failure.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if an internal executor bug (e.g. malformed translator output) increments provider failure counters or triggers a model lockout. Test: inject a translator throw on a healthy account and assert getAccountHealth is unchanged and no lockout entry is created.

PROBLEM: When the selected model is unavailable (404 / model-not-found), the router should try a sibling model in the same family rather than failing the whole request - but only post-error, never speculatively, and without cycling.
MECHANISM: Post-error-only family fallback: explicit family templates, provider-catalog membership checks, lifecycle selectability, and a tried-model set that prevents cycles. Handles model notation variants. Fallback triggers only after a model-unavailable failure classification, not preemptively. [Evidence: open-sse/services/modelFamilyFallback.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Fallback candidates must come from the same family template, be members of the provider catalog, be lifecycle-selectable (not retired), and never repeat a tried model. Fallback never widens beyond the family.
FAILURE_MODEL: If no family sibling is selectable, the original model-unavailable error is returned; fallback failure does not mask the root error.
SECURITY_MODEL: No new credentials are introduced; the fallback uses the same connection. No prompt content is involved in the selection.
SCALING_MODEL: tried-set is per-request O(fallbacks); templates are static data. No cross-request state.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE recovery: same-family fallback as a bounded, post-error recovery inside the authorized envelope - provided the sibling was already authorized.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must add typed capability-compatibility gating: same family does not prove equivalent tools, structured output, reasoning behavior, context window, or data residency. OmniRoute's fallback does not visibly prove capability equivalence, so CRX must require the fallback target to be capability-compatible AND pre-authorized by POLICY, otherwise REJECT the hop.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low for the tried-set/post-error/cycle-avoidance mechanics; Medium to add capability-compatibility checks.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Prevents total failure on model renames/retirements, but only safe with capability gates.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if fallback fires before any error (speculative), revisits a tried model, or selects a model not in the provider catalog. Test: drive the fallback with a scripted unavailable-model error and assert (a) exactly one pre-error attempt, (b) no repeated model ids across the attempt chain, (c) every fallback target present in the catalog.

PROBLEM: Operators need an explicit, auditable order of providers to try when the primary fails - declared up front, not improvised per request.
MECHANISM: Declarative ordered provider chains persisted to SQLite with an in-memory cache. Resolution filters the chain to enabled providers and removes already-tried providers. The chain is data, resolved at request time. [Evidence: src/domain/fallbackPolicy.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: The effective chain is always a subsequence of the declared chain: resolution may only filter (enabled, not-tried), never reorder or append. The declared chain is the complete search space.
FAILURE_MODEL: DB load/save failures are swallowed (best-effort cache), so a DB outage can silently serve a stale chain or an empty chain. Resolution on an empty chain must fail closed with no candidates rather than falling back to an implicit default.
SECURITY_MODEL: Chain declarations contain provider ids only, no secrets. Audit who edits the chain.
SCALING_MODEL: Chain length is operator-bounded; resolution is O(chain). In-memory cache avoids per-request DB reads.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX POLICY input: the ordered fallback chain is part of the authorized execution envelope - POLICY declares 'if primary fails, these (already-authorized) providers may be tried, in this order'.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must make chain persistence canonical: load failure is a typed error that blocks routing (fail closed), not a swallowed best-effort; every resolution should reference the chain version/hash in the receipt.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low. The filter-only resolution semantics are the valuable part; persistence must be hardened.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Turns fallback from emergent behavior into declared, auditable policy.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if resolution ever returns a provider not in the declared chain, reorders the chain, or retries an already-tried provider. Test: property test with random chains/ tried-sets asserting output is always a subsequence of enabled, untried chain members in declared order.

PROBLEM: Repeated provider failures must open a circuit that fails fast, then half-open probes recovery, without scattering ad-hoc failure counters through the codebase.
MECHANISM: A pure, immutable state machine: createAdaptiveCircuit() -> { closed }; observeCircuit(current, 'failure'|'success'|'probe', { failureThreshold default 3, cooldownMs default 60000, reason }) returns a new AdaptiveCircuit with closed/open/half_open states, failureCount/successCount, lastFailureAt/openedAt/halfOpenAt/nextProbeAt timestamps, and reason. Failures increment and open the circuit at threshold (or immediately from half_open); probe transitions open->half_open only after nextProbeAt; any success closes and resets. No I/O, no Date hidden inside (now injectable), no singletons. [Evidence: src/lib/resilience/adaptiveCircuit.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: State transitions are total and deterministic given (state, event, options, now). The circuit never opens on success and never closes on failure. Probe is the only exit from open.
FAILURE_MODEL: There is no persistence: a process restart resets all circuits to closed. Callers needing durable exclusion must persist transitions themselves.
SECURITY_MODEL: No secrets or request data in circuit state; only counts, timestamps, and a reason string. Reason strings must not embed error bodies with credentials.
SCALING_MODEL: O(circuits) memory; per-event cost is a single object spread. Safe to keep one circuit per provider/connection.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE health gating: one pure circuit per (provider, connection) inside the authorized set; transitions recorded into the ExecutionReceipt as routing evidence.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must persist circuit transitions durably (or accept restart-reset explicitly in the threat model) and ensure an open circuit only removes candidates from the authorized set - it must never add or authorize new ones.
INTEGRATION_COST: Very low. Pure functions; lift verbatim and wrap with CRX persistence/receipt hooks.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Small, correct, testable primitive that replaces scattered ad-hoc health flags.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if observeCircuit mutates its input, reads the clock without an injected now, performs I/O, or allows a transition not in {failure->open@threshold, open->half_open@probe-after-cooldown, any->closed@success}. Test: deep-freeze input, run 10k random event sequences with fixed now, assert input unchanged and every transition matches the table.

PROBLEM: A provider that is failing should be temporarily excluded with backoff, re-admitted cautiously, and probed - while a fleet-wide incident (>50% circuits open) should disable exploration entirely.
MECHANISM: SelfHealingManager: score < EXCLUSION_THRESHOLD (0.2) excludes with DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_MS 5min, doubling on repeat up to MAX_COOLDOWN_MS 30min; re-admission requires score >= REENTRY_THRESHOLD (0.3, hysteresis above exclusion) AND cooldown expiry; HALF_OPEN state allows a single probe (isProbe, probeCount tracked); incident mode triggers when >50% of circuits are OPEN (INCIDENT_MODE_THRESHOLD 0.5) and forces exploitation-only (no exploration). [Evidence: open-sse/services/autoCombo/selfHealing.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Exclusion is score-and-circuit driven and temporary; re-admission is strictly harder than exclusion (0.3 > 0.2) to prevent flapping. Incident mode only narrows the candidate set, never widens it.
FAILURE_MODEL: Exclusions are in-memory; a restart clears them (fail-open toward retrying bad providers). If exclusions empty the pool, the engine reintroduces all candidates (engine.ts) - safe only if exclusions are health-based, dangerous if any exclusion encodes a policy boundary.
SECURITY_MODEL: Exclusion reasons are operator-visible strings; keep provider error bodies out of them.
SCALING_MODEL: O(excluded providers) memory; per-request check is a map lookup. Cooldowns are timestamps, no timers.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE resilience: temporary exclusion with hysteresis and incident-mode exploitation-only, applied strictly inside the authorized candidate set.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must tag every exclusion with its basis (health vs policy) and make the empty-pool path fail closed when any exclusion is policy-based: never resurrect a policy-forbidden candidate. OmniRoute's reintroduce-all behavior must be gated on 'all exclusions are health-only'.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low-Medium. The hysteresis/probe/incident mechanics port directly; the empty-pool guard needs a policy-basis tag.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-High. This is the difference between graceful degradation and cascading failure during a provider incident.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if a provider with score in [0.2, 0.3) is re-admitted, if incident mode still explores, or if the empty-pool path reintroduces a candidate excluded for a policy reason. Test: script exclusion at score 0.19, attempt re-admit at 0.25 (must stay excluded); force >50% OPEN and assert exploration rate is 0; mark one exclusion policy-based, empty the pool, assert routing fails closed.

PROBLEM: Given N candidate provider/model/accounts, pick WHERE/HOW an authorized inference executes by explainable weighted scoring over quota, health, cost, latency, task fit, stability, tier, affinity, quality, and reliability - with budget caps and exploration.
MECHANISM: scoreAutoTargets computes per-candidate factors (quota, health, inverse cost, inverse latency, task fit, stability, account tier, affinity, connection density, observed quality, reliability), normalizes DEFAULT_WEIGHTS (sum 1.0), clamps factors, and ranks. engine.ts adds self-healing exclusion, epsilon exploration via Math.random (lines 191, 299, 302), tier rotation, and budget behavior: budgetFallback 'strict' throws BudgetExceededError when nothing fits (lines 32-37, 49-63, 332-333); legacy 'cheapest' default knowingly selects over budget. If exclusions empty the pool, all candidates are reintroduced. [Evidence: open-sse/services/autoCombo/engine.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/services/autoCombo/scoring.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Scoring may only rank a pre-authorized candidate set; it never admits a candidate. Budget 'strict' fails closed; exploration never exceeds the candidate set.
FAILURE_MODEL: Three fail-opens: (1) default 'cheapest' budgetFallback knowingly overspends; (2) Math.random() exploration is non-replayable unless the draw is recorded; (3) empty-pool reintroduction can resurrect policy-excluded candidates. Complexity/prompt classification feeds task fit - it must not become action authorization.
SECURITY_MODEL: Scores contain only numeric factors and candidate ids; no prompts, bodies, or credentials.
SCALING_MODEL: O(candidates x factors) per request; no retained per-request state beyond the selected route.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE: weighted scoring is exactly the WHERE/HOW optimizer - but only over the POLICY-authorized set, with the selected route and its score breakdown written into the receipt.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must (a) default budgetFallback to strict (fail closed on overspend), (b) replace Math.random with a seeded/deterministic draw recorded in the receipt, or record the draw basis, (c) add deterministic tie-breaking in sorting, and (d) gate empty-pool resurrection on health-only exclusions.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium. Scoring math ports; determinism, strict budgets, and the authorized-set precondition are CRX-side requirements.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High. This is the core 'routing optimization decides WHERE/HOW' machinery - valuable only with the authorization boundary hardened.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if the scorer admits a candidate not in its input set, if two identical inputs produce different rankings without a recorded random basis, or if 'strict' budget mode selects an over-budget candidate. Test: fixed candidate set, run 1000 selections, assert identical ranking given identical seed/basis and assert output subset of input.

PROBLEM: Operators need to ask 'what would the router pick?' without spending money or hitting providers - a dry-run that is provably side-effect free.
MECHANISM: POST /api/omniroute/route/preview validates candidates with zod (providerId, modelId, capabilityScore, allocation allow|warn|deny, healthScore, circuit closed|open|half_open, quota enum, latencyMs, errorRate, model/cost preference), runs rankCandidates, and returns candidate scores, factors, reasons, the selected provider, and liveRequestExecuted: false. The handler comment states 'Deterministic routing preview. It never calls an upstream provider.' Allocation 'deny', open circuits, and exhausted quota are ineligible per the routing policy doc. [Evidence: src/app/api/omniroute/route/preview/route.ts @ 18bbb101980c / src/lib/routing/adaptiveRouting.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Preview performs zero upstream model requests and zero state mutation; the same candidate set always yields the same preview. Preview output is advisory and never authorizes execution.
FAILURE_MODEL: Preview is only as honest as its inputs: stale health/quota inputs produce stale previews. It does not verify that the caller is authorized to execute the selected route.
SECURITY_MODEL: Candidates are caller-supplied descriptors; no credentials accepted or needed. Auth is management-level (requireManagementAuth).
SCALING_MODEL: O(candidates) CPU; no retained state. Safe to expose to operators.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX dry-run for POLICY: 'given this authorized set and these health signals, what would ROUTE pick?' - a planning/explainability tool that cannot execute.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must bind preview inputs to the actual POLICY snapshot (authorized set + policy version) so the preview answers the real question, and must never let a preview response be replayed as an execution authorization.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low. The endpoint shape and the liveRequestExecuted:false contract port directly.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Gives operators and evaluators a safe way to interrogate routing without spend; also the natural conformance test for ROUTE determinism.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if the preview path issues any upstream network call or mutates routing/health state. Test: run preview with network stubs that throw and a snapshot of health state before/after; assert identical state and zero stub invocations.

PROBLEM: Every routing decision and attempt outcome must be observable as typed data for debugging, quality feedback, and audit - without slowing the hot path or leaking sensitive content.
MECHANISM: RoutingEvent is a typed struct: requestId, provider, model, strategy, latencyMs, ttftMs, itlMs, input/output tokens, cost, retries, fallbackUsed, outcome (allowlisted union), status, finishReason, connectionId, ts. Explicitly forbidden: prompts, bodies, headers, credentials, account ids. emitRoutingEvent fans out synchronously to registered sinks (memory ring buffer default 500, quality tracker, optional OTLP); each sink must be O(1) with no sync I/O; sink exceptions are swallowed with isolation so one bad sink cannot break the hot path or other sinks. Sinks register via open-sse/services/routing/index.ts. [Evidence: open-sse/services/routing/events.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/services/routing/index.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Events carry routing metadata only - never prompts, bodies, headers, credentials, or account ids. A sink must never block or fail the request path.
FAILURE_MODEL: Sink exceptions are swallowed: a failing sink silently loses events. The default store is a bounded in-memory ring (500) - restarts lose history. This is observability, not durable evidence.
SECURITY_MODEL: The metadata-only contract is the security core: enforce it with a type-level allowlist, not convention. connectionId is present but account ids are excluded by design.
SCALING_MODEL: Bounded by construction: 500-event ring, O(1) sinks, OTel buffer drops oldest under overload (never backpressures).
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ExecutionReceipt shape: RoutingEvent is the prototype of the per-attempt receipt - requestId, provider/model, strategy, timing, tokens, cost, retries, fallback flag, outcome, connection. CRX must make it durable with Run/Mission lineage and policy version.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must (a) persist receipts durably (append-only log keyed by attempt id with parent run id), (b) add policy snapshot hash and authorized-set version to each receipt, (c) replace swallowed sink errors with typed delivery outcomes for audit sinks while keeping best-effort for observability sinks.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium. The event schema and sink-isolation pattern port; durability and lineage are new CRX work.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High. This is the receipt half of the seam; without it CRX cannot prove what the router did.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if any emitted event contains prompt text, request bodies, headers, credentials, or account ids, or if a throwing sink breaks the request path. Test: register a throwing sink and a capturing sink, run requests with secret-bearing bodies, assert responses succeed and captured events contain none of the forbidden fields.

PROBLEM: When a router considers many candidates and picks one, operators need the why: which candidates were dispatched, skipped (with reason), or never reached - per invocation.
MECHANISM: Per-invocation decision trace recording dispatched / skipped / not-reached candidates with an allowlist of skip reasons; excludes sensitive bodies/credentials; random UUID per trace; stored in memory with 30-minute TTL and a 2,000-trace cap. [Evidence: open-sse/services/combo/decisionTrace.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Skip reasons come from a fixed allowlist; traces never contain request bodies or credentials. A trace explains a decision; it does not authorize one.
FAILURE_MODEL: In-memory with 30-min TTL and 2000-trace cap: traces are debugging aids, not evidence. Random UUIDs are not replayable identities.
SECURITY_MODEL: Same metadata-only discipline as routing events; UUIDs are random, not derived from request content.
SCALING_MODEL: Bounded: 2000 traces, 30-min TTL. Per-request cost is O(candidates considered).
CRX_ANALOG: CRX route-decision record: the 'why this provider' attachment to the ExecutionReceipt - considered candidates, skip reasons, final pick. CRX needs it durable and deterministically keyed.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must replace random UUIDs with deterministic attempt ids derived from (run id, attempt sequence), persist traces with the receipt, and extend TTL to the retention policy of mission evidence.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low. The considered/skipped/reason shape ports directly; identity and durability are CRX-side.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Turns 'the router picked X' from an assertion into an inspectable record.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if a trace contains a request body, credentials, or a skip reason outside the allowlist, or if two identical routing decisions produce traces that cannot be correlated by attempt identity. Test: capture traces for scripted decisions and assert field allowlist + reason allowlist conformance.

PROBLEM: Before dispatching, the router should check whether the caller/connection has budget for the estimated cost - and record actual consumption after - across dimensions (requests/tokens/USD) and windows (hourly/5h/daily/weekly/monthly) with per-key fair-share.
MECHANISM: Two-phase quota: enforceQuotaShare pre-request checks per-model caps, pool sharing, weighted fair-share, and dimensions (requests/tokens/USD), returning typed EnforceDecision { allow | block(reason, 429, retryAfterSeconds) }; recordConsumption post-response records actuals. estimateChatTokenCost deterministically estimates input+reserved-output tokens (chars/4 heuristic, x1.1 over-provision, DEFAULT_OUTPUT_ALLOWANCE 1024) and never throws - a broken estimate degrades to 'unknown cost'. Zod-typed dimension model: QuotaUnit percent|requests|tokens|usd, QuotaWindow 5h|hourly|daily|weekly|monthly, Policy hard|soft|burst; PoolUsageSnapshot exposes per-key consumed/fairShare/deficit/borrowing and burn-rate time-to-exhaustion. [Evidence: src/lib/quota/enforce.ts @ 18bbb101980c / src/lib/quota/tokenEstimator.ts @ 18bbb101980c / src/lib/quota/dimensions.ts @ 18bbb101980c / src/lib/quota/types.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Preflight may only deny within declared caps; estimation is advisory and deliberately over-provisions. Post-response recording is the source of truth for consumption, not the estimate.
FAILURE_MODEL: enforce.ts is explicitly fail-open on DB, store, plan, and saturation failures: any infrastructure failure allows the request. As authorization or hard spend safety this is REJECT-grade; as advisory scheduling it is acceptable. A broken token estimate degrades to 'unknown cost' which the scheduler treats as affordable.
SECURITY_MODEL: Quota state is keyed by apiKeyId/connectionId; consumption records must not embed request content. Fail-open paths must be visible in receipts so overspend is auditable.
SCALING_MODEL: Preflight is O(dimensions); consumption recording is async post-response. Store is the scaling bottleneck, not the math.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX POLICY preflight: deterministic cost estimation before ROUTE plus typed allow/block - but CRX must wrap it fail-closed: infrastructure failure blocks (or explicitly degrades with a recorded gap), never silently allows.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must invert the fail-open default: DB/store/plan failure -> typed enforcement-unavailable outcome that POLICY handles (block or explicit operator-approved degrade), and every allow/block decision references the quota snapshot version in the receipt.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium. The two-phase shape, dimension model, and fair-share math port; the failure semantics must be inverted to fail-closed.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-High. Pre-request estimation plus post-response truth is the only sane shape for spend control; the fail-open default is the trap to avoid.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if a request is allowed when the quota store is unreachable without a typed enforcement-unavailable marker in the receipt, or if consumption is recorded from the estimate instead of actual usage. Test: kill the quota store, send requests, assert every receipt carries an explicit enforcement-unavailable marker and no silent allow.

PROBLEM: An operator wants a hard guarantee of zero incremental spend: candidates must prove, per connection, that free allowance remains - from metadata, not provider-name special cases - before ranking, before dispatch, never after.
MECHANISM: Pure, dependency-light filter: candidates pass/fail on carried metadata (freeType, tos, hardStopGuaranteed) plus an injected FreeAccessState { status SAFE|EXHAUSTED|UNKNOWN, remainingFreeAllowance, resetAt, checkedAt } resolved per (provider, connection) by an injected function - the module never touches DB or network. No provider or model name appears in the file. Connection safety: for multi-account candidates, allowedConnectionIds is REWRITTEN to exactly the subset proven SAFE, and downstream routing already intersects against allowedConnectionIds - so 'verified this connection' and 'dispatch used this connection' are the same set by construction. Stale state (checkedAt older than maxStateAgeMs) -> UNKNOWN -> excluded. Fully-exhausted (remaining == 0) fails at any threshold via strict > comparison. [Evidence: open-sse/services/autoCombo/strictZeroCostFilter.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: A candidate is dispatchable only if its specific connection proved SAFE within maxStateAgeMs; UNKNOWN or EXHAUSTED is exclusion. The filter never consults provider identity, only metadata + live state.
FAILURE_MODEL: The live state resolver is injected: if the resolver has no fresh data, the result is terminal UNKNOWN (excluded), not a retry - fail-closed on missing evidence. Staleness is treated as unknown, not as safe.
SECURITY_MODEL: No credentials in the filter; state is allowance metadata only. The now() function is injectable for deterministic tests.
SCALING_MODEL: O(candidates x connections) pure CPU per pool build; state resolution is cached upstream once per pool build. No per-request I/O in the filter itself.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX POLICY hard-constraint enforcement: the shape of a pre-dispatch gate where operator-declared invariants (zero spend, region pinning, capability floors) are enforced on metadata before scoring, with the verified set rewritten into the candidate set by construction.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must record the filter's input state versions (checkedAt per connection) in the receipt so 'was proven SAFE at dispatch' is auditable; and must ensure the constraint set itself comes from POLICY, not from the router's discretion.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low-Medium. The pure-filter + injected-state + allowlist-rewrite pattern ports cleanly; CRX adds receipt binding.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High. This is the cleanest example of a hard constraint enforced at the seam without the router becoming an authorizer: the constraint is declared, the proof is per-connection, and verification equals dispatch by construction.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if a candidate with UNKNOWN/EXHAUSTED state is dispatched, if allowedConnectionIds after filtering still contains an unverified connection that gets used, or if a provider name (rather than metadata) influences the outcome. Test: fixtures with mixed SAFE/UNKNOWN/EXHAUSTED connections asserting exact post-filter allowlists, plus a test with a brand-new provider name carrying correct metadata asserting it passes (autodiscovery contract).

PROBLEM: Route requests through an ordered economic ladder (subscription -> keyless -> free -> cheap -> premium), escalating only when the cheaper rung provably cannot serve - with different fail semantics per rung.
MECHANISM: Explicit rungs with per-rung grouping: subscription-only grouping fails closed on unverifiable quota; thrifty grouping admits unknown quota and can escalate to paid. Each rung individually verifies allowed connections and rewrites allowlists so the verified set is the dispatchable set. [Evidence: open-sse/services/autoCombo/subscriptionLadder.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Escalation only moves down the ladder toward more expensive rungs when the current rung provably cannot serve; it never skips rungs and never escalates on the basis of prompt content.
FAILURE_MODEL: Subscription-only grouping fails closed (unverifiable quota -> no serve); thrifty grouping fails open toward escalation (unknown quota admitted). The grouping choice is the risk decision and must be explicit.
SECURITY_MODEL: No credentials in ladder logic; connection verification is by id against quota state.
SCALING_MODEL: O(rungs x candidates); verification is cached per pool build.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE economic ordering: POLICY declares the ladder and which groupings are authorized; ROUTE walks it. The 'paid escalation authorized?' question belongs to POLICY, not to the router.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must make the grouping choice (fail-closed subscription-only vs escalating thrifty) an explicit, receipt-recorded POLICY field; the router must not silently pick thrifty.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low. The rung ordering + per-rung verification + allowlist rewrite ports directly.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Ordered economic routing with explicit fail semantics is the sane way to offer 'cheap first' without surprise spend.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if the router escalates to a paid rung when POLICY authorized subscription-only, or dispatches on a connection the rung did not verify. Test: policy=subscriptions-only with unverifiable quota must fail closed; thrifty policy must show the escalation step and its basis in the trace.

PROBLEM: Protect the execution seam from overload with admission control that is explicit about modes (off/shadow/enforce), cost-aware, and honest about local vs upstream pressure.
MECHANISM: Weighted adaptive admission controller with off/shadow/enforce modes, typed leases, queue outcomes, deadlines, pressure signals, cost accounting, and per-tenant virtual lanes; explicitly distinguishes upstream errors from local capacity failures. estimateAdmissionCost is a pure, bounded, deterministic cost estimator from transparent quanta (body bytes, tokens, messages, tools, fanout, streaming class) with validated positive safe-integer config. checkQueueAdmission is a pure opt-in queue-depth gate returning a typed RATE_LIMIT_QUEUE_FULL error branded (WeakMap) as local - not upstream - so health/routing decisions attribute pressure correctly. [Evidence: open-sse/services/admission/ @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/services/admission/cost.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/services/rateLimitManager/admission.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Admission decisions are capacity decisions only: they shed load, they never authorize. Local pressure is always labeled local; upstream errors never count against local capacity.
FAILURE_MODEL: Shadow mode observes without enforcing; enforce mode rejects with typed errors carrying retry guidance. Queue-full rejection is opt-in (default disabled) to preserve existing behavior.
SECURITY_MODEL: Cost features are sizes/counts only; no request content in admission state. Per-tenant lanes isolate tenants' pressure from each other.
SCALING_MODEL: Bounded: queue depth caps, cost caps (maxRequestCost), typed leases with deadlines. No unbounded queues by default.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE capacity guard: admission sits downstream of authorization and upstream of dispatch - it decides whether the seam has capacity for an authorized request, never whether the request is allowed.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must keep admission strictly downstream of POLICY authorization in the pipeline order and record the admission mode and lease in the receipt; a request blocked by admission is 'authorized but shed', not 'denied'.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low-Medium. Modes, typed leases, local-vs-upstream error branding, and the pure cost estimator port well.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Prevents retry storms and overload collapse; the local-vs-upstream error branding is the subtle, valuable part.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if an upstream 5xx is counted as local pressure, if shadow mode ever rejects, or if a queue-full error is attributed to the provider in health scoring. Test: inject upstream failures and assert local pressure metrics unchanged; run shadow mode under overload and assert zero rejections; assert the WeakMap brand distinguishes local vs upstream 429s in health inputs.

PROBLEM: Provider quality feedback must improve routing without ever manufacturing a quality judgment the system did not observe - and operational health must not be confused with output value.
MECHANISM: v2 quality separates operational from semantic: operational is derived from the routing hot path (HTTP 4xx/5xx, connection failures, 429s, malformed responses, stream interruptions, finish_reason=length, zero-output successes, latency/TTFT EWMA); semantic is ONLY ever produced by an evaluator via setSemanticQuality(), is null until one provides it, and never leaks into the operational score. 429 is treated as transient (0.5, neutral-positive) not as failure. Confidence blending: score = 0.5 + (samples/50 clamped) * (operational - 0.5), so cold providers score neutral 0.5 and lucky streaks cannot dominate. Quality is a soft adaptive preference; hard exclusion stays with the resilience stack (circuit OPEN, quota exhausted, auth failure). [Evidence: open-sse/services/routing/quality.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: The system never asserts output quality it did not measure: semantic is null without an evaluator, and 0.5 means 'no evidence', never 'mediocre'. Operational signals never masquerade as quality judgments.
FAILURE_MODEL: Evaluator absent -> quality falls back to neutral; routing is unaffected. One isolated failure does not destroy a healthy provider (EWMA).
SECURITY_MODEL: Quality state is per (provider, model) numeric state; no request content. Semantic scores from evaluators must be labeled with evaluator identity.
SCALING_MODEL: O(providers x models) EWMA state; O(1) per event update. Bounded counters.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE feedback: operational quality as a soft routing preference with confidence blending; semantic quality only from an explicit evaluator - CRX must never let the router grade its own homework.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must record evaluator identity and confidence with any semantic score in the receipt, and keep hard exclusion (policy/health) independent of quality scores so a quality dip can never disable an authorized provider.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low. The operational/semantic split, 429 handling, and confidence blending port directly.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium-High. This is the anti-Goodhart pattern: it lets routing learn without letting the router invent quality facts.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if a semantic score appears without an evaluator call, if a 429 depresses the operational score as a failure, or if a quality dip alone hard-excludes a provider. Test: run with no evaluator and assert semantic is null everywhere; inject 429s and assert operational stays neutral-positive; drive quality to 0 and assert the provider remains selectable (de-preferenced, not excluded).

PROBLEM: Retry, rotation, and fallback decisions need a single typed vocabulary for what went wrong - distinguishing 'retryable' from 'terminal' and 'rate limited' from 'quota exhausted'.
MECHANISM: classifyProviderFailure maps (providerId, connectionId?, statusCode?, code?, message?, retryAfter?) to ProviderFailure { type: authentication_error | rate_limit | quota_exhausted | timeout | network_error | provider_5xx | invalid_request | model_unavailable | permission_error | unknown; retryable: boolean }. Key distinctions: 429 with quota/insufficient-balance language -> quota_exhausted (NOT retryable); 429 otherwise -> rate_limit (retryable); timeouts/5xx/network -> retryable; 401/403/auth patterns -> terminal auth errors; 404/model-not-found -> model_unavailable (drives family fallback, not retry). [Evidence: src/lib/resilience/failureClassification.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Classification is deterministic on its inputs; retryable=true is the only license to retry. quota_exhausted is never retryable - retrying it is pure waste.
FAILURE_MODEL: Unknown inputs classify as unknown/non-retryable: fail-closed toward not retrying. Message-pattern matching is heuristic; status codes take precedence where present.
SECURITY_MODEL: Operates on status codes and error text; no credentials involved. Avoid persisting raw error bodies containing key material.
SCALING_MODEL: Pure function, O(input) regex work, no state. Safe on the hot path.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX attempt-outcome vocabulary: every ProviderAttempt receipt carries a typed failure classification; retry/rotation/fallback policy keys off the type, not on ad-hoc string matching scattered through the codebase.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX should treat the classification as the single choke point: the pipeline, health scorer, and fallback logic all consume ProviderFailure, and any new failure signal is added here, not inline.
INTEGRATION_COST: Very low. Pure function; lift verbatim.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Small but load-bearing: every recovery decision in the seam keys off this vocabulary.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if a quota-exhausted 429 is marked retryable, if an auth failure is marked retryable, or if identical inputs produce different classifications. Test: table-driven cases over status codes and message patterns asserting (type, retryable) pairs, including the quota-vs-ratelimit 429 split.

PROBLEM: OAuth token refresh must not loop forever against a dead provider: bound the retries, back off, circuit-break per provider, and short-circuit unrecoverable errors so health checks can deactivate the account.
MECHANISM: refreshWithRetry wraps refresh with exponential backoff, a 30s per-attempt timeout, and a per-provider circuit breaker (5 consecutive failures -> 30min pause; isProviderBlocked). Unrecoverable refresh errors (invalid_grant, refresh_token_reused, ...) short-circuit retries immediately so the HealthCheck can deactivate the account instead of looping every 60s. Circuit status is exposable for diagnostics (getCircuitBreakerStatus). [Evidence: open-sse/services/tokenRefresh/circuitBreaker.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/services/tokenRefresh/rotationMap.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Refresh attempts are bounded in count, duration, and frequency; unrecoverable errors never retried. A broken credential deactivates the account; it does not spin the refresh loop.
FAILURE_MODEL: Circuit state is in-memory: a restart clears the breaker and refresh resumes. Refresh failure must surface as account-unhealthy, never as a silent stall of the request.
SECURITY_MODEL: Refresh tokens are the most sensitive credential in the system: confine refresh to this module, never log token material, and ensure deactivation actually revokes/stops use of the credential.
SCALING_MODEL: O(providers) breaker state; per-refresh cost is bounded by timeout x attempts.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX credential-layer support for long-lived missions: bounded refresh with circuit breaking keeps the execution seam alive across token expiry without turning a dead credential into a hot loop.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must make refresh outcomes part of the receipt evidence (token refreshed at T, or account deactivated for unrecoverable error) and ensure a refreshed credential only serves requests within the still-valid authorization envelope.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low-Medium. Backoff + per-provider breaker + unrecoverable short-circuit ports directly; CRX adds receipt binding.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. The unrecoverable-error short-circuit is the valuable subtlety: distinguishing 'try again later' from 'this credential is dead'.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if an invalid_grant error is retried more than once, if refresh attempts exceed the bound, or if a circuit-broken provider still attempts refresh. Test: script invalid_grant and assert exactly one attempt then account-deactivation signal; script 5 consecutive failures and assert isProviderBlocked true for 30min.

PROBLEM: Operators and auditors need the real routing decisions - not a recomputation, not a sample - with the quality state that drove them, under the same auth as the rest of management.
MECHANISM: GET /v1/explain/routing returns the most recent RoutingEvents (bounded in-memory ring, newest first) plus the per-provider/model quality snapshot with classifyQuality labels, OTel stats, and sink registration state. Comment: 'This is REAL decision data - the events were emitted by the request hot path, not recomputed after the fact.' Safety contract: only routing metadata (provider/model/strategy/timing/tokens/outcome/status/finish_reason); never prompts, bodies, headers, credentials, accounts. Auth mirrors /v1/combos (Bearer key or dashboard session; anonymous only when REQUIRE_API_KEY=false on single-user local). Cache-Control: no-store. [Evidence: src/app/api/v1/explain/routing/route.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: The endpoint reports decisions; it cannot change them. Reported data is restricted to routing metadata by construction.
FAILURE_MODEL: Events are the bounded in-memory ring: history is limited and lost on restart. Quality snapshot is point-in-time.
SECURITY_MODEL: Metadata-only contract enforced at the event schema level; auth mirrors management endpoints. limit param is clamped 1..500.
SCALING_MODEL: O(limit) response; ring is bounded. No per-request retained state.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX audit surface for the ROUTE step: 'show me what the router actually decided and why' - the human-readable counterpart to the durable receipt log.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must back the endpoint with the durable receipt store (not just the ring) for anything beyond recent debugging, and keep the metadata-only contract as a type-level guarantee.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low. The endpoint shape, auth mirroring, and metadata-only contract port directly.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Makes routing legible to operators and auditors; the 'real decisions, not recomputed' property is what makes it trustworthy.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if the endpoint returns anything outside routing metadata, recomputes decisions instead of reading emitted events, or is reachable without auth when REQUIRE_API_KEY=true. Test: capture a live event, fetch the endpoint, assert the event appears verbatim; fuzz the response for prompt/body/credential fields.

PROBLEM: Model-to-task suitability scores must be evidence-graded: user overrides beat arena ELO beats catalog tiers beats a hand table beats a neutral baseline - and 'unknown' must never read as 'bad'.
MECHANISM: Layered resolution (highest to lowest): (1) user override from model_intelligence where source='user_override'; (2) arena ELO (source='arena_elo'), with inheritance via resolveScoresAs and vendor-retired veto; (3) models.dev tier from model_capabilities with retired-id veto (a retired id never earns a tier score); (4) small static FITNESS_TABLE of versioned model ids only - family patterns banned because they scored retired members above live flagships; (5) wildcard baseline 0.5. Explicit doctrine: 0.5 means 'no evidence', NOT 'mediocre model', and must never be read as a quality claim. Build fails (scripts/check/check-model-lifecycle.mjs) when a table row matches a vendor-retired id. [Evidence: open-sse/services/autoCombo/taskFitness.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Every score carries its provenance layer; unknown is always the neutral midpoint, never a penalty. Retired models can never earn a positive score from stale table data.
FAILURE_MODEL: DB-backed layers degrade to lower layers when data is absent; absence of evidence resolves to 0.5, never to exclusion.
SECURITY_MODEL: No request content in fitness data; user overrides are operator data, auditable.
SCALING_MODEL: Static table is tiny; DB lookups are cached. Per-request cost is a layered lookup.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE task-fit factor: evidence-graded capability scoring where the score's provenance travels with it into the receipt - and where unknown capability is neutral, not disqualifying (disqualification is POLICY's job).
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must separate 'capability unknown' (neutral score, POLICY decides if acceptable) from 'capability insufficient' (POLICY exclusion). OmniRoute's layering is the pattern; CRX adds the policy-binding.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low. The layering and the 0.5-means-no-evidence doctrine port directly.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Prevents the quiet, common failure where 'we have no data on this model' silently becomes 'this model is bad'.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if a retired model id receives a score above 0.5 from any layer, if an unknown model scores anything but 0.5, or if a score lacks provenance. Test: feed retired ids and unknown ids through the resolver asserting scores and provenance labels.

PROBLEM: The execution seam must treat a local model (Ollama) as just another provider: same routing, same receipts, different wire destination - including local-first privacy postures.
MECHANISM: Local models register through the same provider registry (ollama-cloud, g4f-ollama descriptors), with ollamaModels.ts declaring the local model inventory (name, digest, format, family, parameter_size, quantization) and ollamaTransform.ts normalizing the Ollama wire shape into the canonical flow. No special-case routing path: a local endpoint is a provider with a URL. [Evidence: open-sse/config/ollamaModels.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/config/providers/registry/ollama-cloud/index.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/config/providers/registry/g4f-ollama/index.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/utils/ollamaTransform.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: Routing treats local and cloud providers identically; any local-first preference is expressed as scoring/policy weights, not as a code fork.
FAILURE_MODEL: Local daemon down -> provider failure like any other (connection failure classification); no special fallback unless POLICY declares one.
SECURITY_MODEL: Local routing keeps prompts on-machine: a privacy win, but receipts must still avoid persisting prompt content. Model digests in the inventory double as integrity references.
SCALING_MODEL: Same per-request cost as any provider; inventory is static data.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX PROVIDER step: the proof that the seam is genuinely replaceable - Ollama, cloud APIs, and coding-agent-compatible endpoints are all just descriptors + translators. Enables local-first mission execution.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must add data-residency/capability declarations to the local descriptor (context window, tool support) so ROUTE can prefer local for sensitive missions as a POLICY rule, not a hack.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low. Register local endpoints as providers; reuse the translator and receipt machinery.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium. Makes 'run it locally' a routing decision instead of a separate system.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if local-model requests bypass the policy pipeline, skip receipts, or take a code path that cloud requests cannot take. Test: route identical authorized requests to a local and a cloud provider and assert identical receipt schema and identical policy-gate traversal.

PROBLEM: Keyless / anonymous provider access needs a pool of ephemeral sessions with lifecycle management: active, cooldown, dead - with per-session health, inflight tracking, and jittered backoff.
MECHANISM: Typed session lifecycle: SessionStatus active|cooldown|dead; SessionState tracks id, fingerprint, inflight, total/successful/failed requests, consecutiveFails, cooldownUntil, createdAt, lastUsedAt. PoolConfig is hot-reloadable (min/max sessions, cooldown base/max/jitter, request timeout/jitter). PoolStats exposes real-time health snapshots. Sessions rotate on failure with cooldownBase 1s doubling to cooldownMax 30s plus jitter. [Evidence: open-sse/services/sessionPool/types.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: A session serves traffic only in active status; cooldown and dead sessions are excluded from selection. consecutiveFails drives cooldown; recovery requires successful use.
FAILURE_MODEL: Pool state is in-memory; a restart rebuilds the pool. Dead sessions are replaced up to maxSessions.
SECURITY_MODEL: Sessions carry browser fingerprints (UA, accept-language, sec-ch-ua) for anonymous endpoints. CRX must NOT harvest fingerprint rotation as an anti-detection technique; the harvestable part is the lifecycle state machine, not the fingerprinting. Fingerprint material must never be presented as a real user identity.
SCALING_MODEL: O(sessions) memory bounded by maxSessions (default 20); per-request selection O(pool).
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ROUTE session management for credential-less providers: the active/cooldown/dead lifecycle with inflight caps is a sound connection-pool pattern for any pooled execution resource.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must strip the browser-fingerprint emulation (or explicitly scope it to providers whose ToS permit anonymous programmatic access) and bind pooled sessions to the authorized provider set; an anonymous session must never become a way to reach a non-authorized provider.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low for the lifecycle types and pool config; the fingerprinting must be deliberately excluded or re-scoped.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Low-Medium. Useful pool mechanics; the value is in the state machine, and the risk is in the fingerprinting.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified if a cooldown or dead session is selected for dispatch, or if inflight exceeds the pool's accounting. Test: drive sessions to dead via scripted failures and assert selection excludes them; assert PoolStats inflight matches actual concurrent dispatches.

PROBLEM: When the primary provider fails with a billing-flavored error, the system redirects the request to a free-tier model so the user still gets an answer.
MECHANISM: emergencyFallback.ts: on error-body keyword match (including broad terms like 'billing', line 50), optionally redirect to a hardcoded free-tier model - default provider 'nvidia', model 'openai/gpt-oss-120b' at $0.00/M tokens (lines 6, 39-40). Default-enabled; skips tool requests by default. The redirect destination is NOT drawn from the authorized candidate set - it is a fixed constant chosen by the router at failure time. [Evidence: open-sse/services/emergencyFallback.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: VIOLATED: the router invents a new authorized provider/model because a billing string appeared in an error body. Routing optimization decided WHETHER (to execute on nvidia/gpt-oss-120b) and WHERE outside any authorization envelope. Keyword matching on error text is not authorization; a fixed fallback constant is not a policy.
FAILURE_MODEL: If the keyword match misfires (any error mentioning 'billing'), requests are silently diverted to the fixed model. Tool requests are skipped, but plain requests are not.
SECURITY_MODEL: The redirect sends the user's prompt to a provider the operator never authorized for that request - a data-routing and spend-authority violation in one.
SCALING_MODEL: O(1) keyword scan per failed request.
CRX_ANALOG: None. CRX must never implement this: a billing-flavored error is a typed quota_exhausted failure (see OR_FAILURE_CLASSIFICATION) that POLICY handles - e.g. by failing closed, queuing, or selecting from the pre-authorized fallback chain. The router must not have a secret fixed destination.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: No delta: do not adapt. If CRX ever wants a free-tier safety net, POLICY declares the destination explicitly per mission, with capability compatibility proven - at which point it is just OR_DECLARATIVE_FALLBACK_CHAINS, not this.
INTEGRATION_COST: N/A - rejected.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Negative: adopting it would punch a router-controlled hole in the authorization envelope, diverting prompts to an unauthorized provider on a keyword match.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Falsified (as a harvestable mechanism) by construction: demonstrate a request whose authorized set is {anthropic/claude-only} being executed on nvidia/openai/gpt-oss-120b after an error containing the substring 'billing'. The test passes (mechanism fires), which is exactly why the class is REJECT.

PROBLEM: The router should sometimes try non-top candidates to discover better routes (epsilon exploration) and recover gracefully when exclusions empty the pool.
MECHANISM: engine.ts: exploration via Math.random() (lines 191, 299, 302) for weighted tier choice and random candidate picks; if exclusions empty the pool, all candidates are reintroduced. There is no seeded RNG, no recorded random basis, and no deterministic tie-breaker in scoring sort - so the same inputs can yield different routes with no audit trail of why. [Evidence: open-sse/services/autoCombo/engine.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: VIOLATED AS-IS: non-replayable routing decisions cannot produce CRX-grade receipts, and empty-pool resurrection can reintroduce candidates excluded for policy reasons, letting optimization override authorization.
FAILURE_MODEL: Exploration rate is configurable, but the randomness source is not. Incident mode (>50% OPEN) disables exploration - the one deterministic guardrail.
SECURITY_MODEL: Non-determinism itself is not a secret leak, but unrecorded draws make audits unverifiable.
SCALING_MODEL: O(1) per draw; no state retained - which is precisely the problem.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX must not harvest this as-is. The adaptable core is 'bounded exploration inside the authorized set with a recorded basis' - but the recording is load-bearing, not optional.

PROBLEM: Route simple prompts to cheap models and complex/tool-heavy prompts to stronger ones by classifying prompt complexity and tool presence.

In CRX terms, tier movement changes the authorized execution profile, which is a POLICY decision, not a routing optimization.
FAILURE_MODEL: Fail-open on classifier error means a misclassified prompt silently gets a different tier with no marker.

PROBLEM: OmniRoute also hosts agent-orchestration surfaces alongside inference routing: ACP (spawning CLI agents like codex/claude/goose as child processes via stdin/stdout JSON-RPC; manager.ts AcpSession with 1MiB bounded buffers), an MCP server (tool surfaces with per-tool scope enforcement, scopeEnforcement.ts, namespace-scoped matching), A2A task lifecycle (submitted->working->completed|failed|cancelled with UUIDs, event logging, TTL, concurrent limits), and a pipeline router (classify intent -> select pipeline template -> execute multi-stage pipelines wrapping handleChatCore).
MECHANISM: These are orchestration and tool/action authorities: they decide WHAT agents do, WHICH tools can be called, and HOW multi-step work unfolds. The CRX model-router seam is MODEL REQUEST -> POLICY -> ROUTE -> PROVIDER -> RECEIPT for a single authorized inference: WHERE/HOW it executes, never WHETHER an action is authorized. Importing ACP process-spawning, MCP tool invocation, A2A task orchestration, or multi-stage pipelines into the router would make the router an orchestration authority - the exact boundary violation this lane forbids (HARVEST_CLASS=REJECT for any mechanism blurring it). The MCP scope-enforcement itself is sound authorization-for-tools, but it belongs to the tool surface, not to inference routing. [Evidence: src/lib/acp/manager.ts @ 18bbb101980c / src/lib/acp/registry.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/mcp-server/scopeEnforcement.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/mcp-server/index.ts @ 18bbb101980c / src/lib/a2a/taskManager.ts @ 18bbb101980c / src/lib/a2a/routingLogger.ts @ 18bbb101980c / src/lib/a2a/taskExecution.ts @ 18bbb101980c / open-sse/services/autoCombo/pipelineRouter.ts @ 18bbb101980c]
INVARIANT: The inference routing seam never triggers a child-process spawn, a tool call, or a task-state transition. Orchestration surfaces consume the execution seam as a client; the seam never calls upward into orchestration.
FAILURE_MODEL: Each surface has its own failure modes (child-process lifecycle, tool scope mismatch, task TTL expiry); none may fail over into or degrade the inference routing path.
SECURITY_MODEL: ACP spawns local binaries (supply-chain and sandboxing risk); MCP tools carry caller scopes verified per call; A2A tasks cross trust boundaries. All three stay outside the inference seam's trust perimeter.
SCALING_MODEL: Independent scaling per surface; no shared state with the routing hot path.
CRX_ANALOG: Negative: these surfaces are what the router must NOT become. CRX orchestration authority (missions, tools, approvals) lives above the execution seam; the seam stays a replaceable WHERE/HOW router. Document the boundary, do not import the machinery.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: No adaptation inside the seam. If CRX needs A2A/MCP interop, it belongs in the orchestration layer above POLICY, consuming the execution seam as a client - never inside ROUTE.
INTEGRATION_COST: N/A - rejected for the seam.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Boundary clarity: naming exactly what stays out of the seam is what keeps the seam replaceable and the authorization boundary intact.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Boundary test: assert that no module under the CRX ROUTE seam imports ACP/MCP/A2A/pipeline modules (static import check), and that a request traversing the seam cannot trigger a child-process spawn, tool call, or task-state transition. Any such path fails the test - and the architecture.
